title: Company Culture as an Operating System

parts.visual:
A startup boasts about its 'Culture' because it has free beer, beanbag chairs, and a ping pong table. But when a server crashes at 2 AM, no one logs in to fix it. The company dies.

The Core Definition:
1. Culture is not perks. Culture is not posters on the wall.
2. Culture is the Operating System: It is the set of unspoken rules that dictate how employees behave when the CEO is not in the room. It is how decisions are made under extreme pressure. It is who gets promoted, and who gets fired.
parts.audio: You do not build a culture by writing a mission statement. You build a culture by firing your top salesperson because they lied to a customer. Actions, especially painful ones, are the only things that program the cultural operating system.

questions.question: A CEO claims their core cultural value is 'Innovation'. But when an engineer tries a radical new idea and it fails, the CEO screams at them in front of the team. What is the *actual* culture?
options: A culture of Fear and Compliance. Words are meaningless. The CEO's reaction to failure programmed every other employee to never take a risk again. The culture is what you tolerate and what you punish.
questions.correct_answer: A culture of Fear and Compliance. Words are meaningless. The CEO's reaction to failure programmed every other employee to never take a risk again. The culture is what you tolerate and what you punish.

questions.question: Listen to the famous Netflix 'Keeper Test'. How do they define a high-performance culture?
questions.tts_text: If one of your employees told you they were leaving for a competitor tomorrow, would you fight hard to keep them? If the answer is no, you should give them severance and fire them right now.
options: Radical Talent Density. Netflix treats its culture like a professional sports team, not a family. You only keep the absolute best players at every position. Adequate performance gets a generous severance package.
questions.correct_answer: Radical Talent Density. Netflix treats its culture like a professional sports team, not a family. You only keep the absolute best players at every position. Adequate performance gets a generous severance package.
questions.explanation: A sports team plays to win.

questions.question: Why is it critical for early-stage founders to explicitly define their culture by employee number 20?
options: Because culture scales organically, whether you control it or not. The first 20 employees become the managers of the next 200. If the first 20 are chaotic and toxic, they will hire 200 chaotic, toxic people. You cannot fix it later.
questions.correct_answer: Because culture scales organically, whether you control it or not. The first 20 employees become the managers of the next 200. If the first 20 are chaotic and toxic, they will hire 200 chaotic, toxic people. You cannot fix it later.
questions.explanation: The DNA is set early. You cannot change it once the organism grows.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Culture eats strategy for breakfast' mean?
options: You can have the most brilliant, perfectly calculated mathematical business strategy in the world. But if your team's culture is lazy, selfish, or paralyzed by politics, they will never be able to execute it.
questions.correct_answer: You can have the most brilliant, perfectly calculated mathematical business strategy in the world. But if your team's culture is lazy, selfish, or paralyzed by politics, they will never be able to execute it.
questions.explanation: Execution requires a healthy operating system.
